_note: OpenRouter twin of the B0 panel (2026-10-10). Future boards run on OpenRouter; this is their baseline.
It is NOT the local panel: providers serve fp8/bf16/int4 weights, not the MLX 8-bit / Q8_0 / PQ2_0 files
the local boards pinned by sha256, so pair later OpenRouter boards with this twin, never with the local B0.
ONE PROVIDER PER MODEL, pinned (provider.order + allow_fallbacks:false), chosen 2026-10-10 from
/api/v1/models/<id>/endpoints for: known quantisation, prompt caching, seed support, and an output cap
as near the local 96,000 as that provider allows. A provider change is a new stamp for the board.
qwen3.6-35b-a3b  AkashML    fp8   cap 235,929 -> 96,000   cache read $0.05 (in $0.10, out $0.90)
qwen3.6-27b      Chutes     fp8   cap  65,536             cache read $0.03 (in $0.30, out $2.00)
qwen3.5-9b       Parasail   bf16  cap 235,929 -> 96,000   no caching offered at bf16 (in $0.10, out $0.25)
bonsai-2-27b     Darkbloom  int4  cap  32,768 (only provider)  cache read $0.037 (in $0.075, out $0.50)
devstral-small-2 and prism-coder-7b are not on OpenRouter.
CACHING. The guide is the shared prefix of every prompt, so a pinned provider with prefix caching reads
it from cache after the first request; usage.include makes the reply report cached tokens, which the
harness records per attempt. Verify cached_tokens > 0 in a smoke run before a board.
seed 42 is set here because --seed-base applies to self-hosted destinations only; repeat r sends 42+r.
stop is null: these are reasoning models and the end marker can fire inside the reasoning.
The key comes from OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment; never put it in this file.
